questions.question: Describe the process of knocking on a guest door to deliver a requested housekeeping service, assuming the guest responds to your knock on the door and opens it.
guidance: Answer may address:
Knock on door using your knuckles.
Announce ‘Housekeeping’.
Greet the guest when they open the door.
Identify yourself and explain the service you are there to provide.
Respond in accordance with guest directions and/or actions.
If they indicate for you to enter the room, thank them and do so – follow their directions or use common sense about where to start providing the service you have arrived to perform.
Thank the guest when finished and ask if there is anything else they want.
Get guest signature (if needed) for items or services provided.
Leave, closing the door behind you.
answer_points: Knock on door using your knuckles.
Announce ‘Housekeeping’.
Greet the guest when they open the door.
Identify yourself and explain the service you are there to provide.
Respond in accordance with guest directions and/or actions.
If they indicate for you to enter the room, thank them and do so – follow their directions or use common sense about where to start providing the service you have arrived to perform.
Thank the guest when finished and ask if there is anything else they want.
Get guest signature (if needed) for items or services provided.
Leave, closing the door behind you.

questions.question: Describe the protocol housekeeping staff should follow when accessing a guest room to provide a requested service: describe the process from start to finish assuming a guest does not open the door in response to your knock.
guidance: Answer must address:
Knock on door with knuckles and announce ‘Housekeeping’.
Wait 10 seconds and repeat.
Wait another 10 seconds and repeat again.
Use your floor key/card to open door slightly and announce ‘Housekeeping’ again.
Enter room slowly again announcing ‘Housekeeping’ and be aware guest may be sleeping or in the bathroom.
If no one is present, provide the requested service and leave, closing the door behind you.
If a guest is present and, say, asleep:
leave quietly

leave without waking the guest -  if you are here to provide a service make sure you return later or notify Floor Housekeeper or Executive Housekeeper that the requested service could not be provided (so it can be followed-up and provide later).
answer_points: Knock on door with knuckles and announce ‘Housekeeping’.
Wait 10 seconds and repeat.
Wait another 10 seconds and repeat again.
Use your floor key/card to open door slightly and announce ‘Housekeeping’ again.
Enter room slowly again announcing ‘Housekeeping’ and be aware guest may be sleeping or in the bathroom.
If no one is present, provide the requested service and leave, closing the door behind you.
If a guest is present and, say, asleep:
leave quietly

leave without waking the guest -  if you are here to provide a service make sure you return later or notify Floor Housekeeper or Executive Housekeeper that the requested service could not be provided (so it can be followed-up and provide later).

questions.question: List five (5) protocols housekeeping staff should follow when interacting with guests while providing housekeeping services.
guidance: Answer may address, but not limited to, five of the following:
Adhere to any house rules for the individual establishment that may apply to this situation.
Smile.
Give a pleasant and short greeting or acknowledgment of the guest.
Use ‘Sir’ or ‘Madam’ when talking with them.
Do not initiate conversation.
Allow the guest to determine the length and nature of the exchange.
Provide requested advice and information promptly, checking the guest has understood what you have told them.
Refer guests to Concierge or nominated other staff member where you cannot assist them as necessary and/or additional information is required.

questions.question: Why is it necessary to use a disinfectant when cleaning nominated areas of a guest room?
guidance: Answer must address:
To kill bacteria
answer_points: To kill bacteria

questions.question: What are three (3) indications that pests might be in a guest room?
guidance: Answer may address, but not limited to, three of the following:
Pest droppings
Damaged food packages
Dead or live pests
Cobwebs or sacs
answer_instructions: Answer may address, but not limited to, three of the following:
answer_points: Pest droppings
Damaged food packages
Dead or live pests
Cobwebs or sacs

questions.question: What are the three (3) key requirements housekeeping staff must adhere to when handling guest property?
guidance: Answer must address:
Handle as little as possible.
Treat it with respect.
Send it to lost property if left in a guest room once they have checked out.
Complete an entry in the Lost and Found Register.
answer_points: Handle as little as possible.
Treat it with respect.
Send it to lost property if left in a guest room once they have checked out.
Complete an entry in the Lost and Found Register.

questions.question: You are servicing a guest room and the guest has open books, sheets of paper and a laptop on the table – they are obviously in the middle of working on something: how should you deal with this situation?
guidance: Answer must address:
Leave it alone – do not tidy the table; do not touch or move anything.
answer_points: Leave it alone – do not tidy the table; do not touch or move anything.

questions.question: What are three (3) things housekeeping staff must do to fulfil the privacy expectations guests have when they stay in an accommodation room?
guidance: Answer may address, but not limited to, three of the following:
Not read any material the guest leaves lying around in their room
Not go through their belongings to find out information about the guest
Not solicit information from the guest

Not disclose or pass on any information they have about the guest to others except the Executive Housekeeper and only then on request or if there is suspicion an offence or illegal activity is involved

answer_points: Not read any material the guest leaves lying around in their room
Not go through their belongings to find out information about the guest
Not solicit information from the guest

Not disclose or pass on any information they have about the guest to others except the Executive Housekeeper and only then on request or if there is suspicion an offence or illegal activity is involved

Maintain guest confidentiality.
Not disclose guest information.
Handle food safely.
Follow work, health and safety requirements.
Wear PPE as required.
Dispose of substances safely following procedures.

Maintain guest confidentiality.
Not disclose guest information.
Handle food safely.
Follow work, health and safety requirements.
Wear PPE as required.

Exposure to sharps
Exposure to blood, faeces and urine

questions.question: What is standard practice when cleaning a guest room to prevent cross-contamination of bacteria from the bathroom or bedroom areas to the mini-bar or kitchen areas?
guidance: Answer must address:
Use colour-coded cloths for each area.
Use disposable cloths in the bathroom/bedroom and then dispose of them before using fresh disposable cloths in the mini-bar/kitchen area.
answer_points: Use colour-coded cloths for each area.
Use disposable cloths in the bathroom/bedroom and then dispose of them before using fresh disposable cloths in the mini-bar/kitchen area.

questions.question: Why is it necessary to clean all food contact surfaces in a guest room with clean cloths?
guidance: Answer must address:
To prevent potential food contamination being caused through cross-contamination.
answer_points: To prevent potential food contamination being caused through cross-contamination.

questions.question: What are three (3) key procedures involved in the cleaning of televisions and remotes?
guidance: Answer should address three of the following:
Turn off electricity at power-point.
Dust television edges, vents and screen with dry micro-fibre cloth .
Spot clean smudges with electronics wipe (never spray glass cleaners).
Sanitise remote control using approved sanitising wipe.

Turn off electricity at power-point.
Dust television edges, vents and screen with dry micro-fibre cloth .
Spot clean smudges with electronics wipe (never spray glass cleaners).
Sanitise remote control using approved sanitising wipe.

Remove, if possible, the faulty item from the room and contact maintenance for collection.
Place a warning sign, such as ‘Out of Service, Do not use’ on a faulty item.
Report to Supervisor.
Contact the Maintenance Department.
Complete a Maintenance Report/ Maintenance Requisition Form.

questions.question: What are three (3) actions you might be expected to take when storing cleaning agents and equipment at the end of a service period?

Leave all equipment, including trolleys, cleaned to hygienic and organisational standards.
Store chemicals separately and in a cool environment.
Store electrical equipment in dry areas.

Do not store equipment above shoulder height.
